answer: Anchor each identity to one pressure sensor lowered onto a single ledge of an ocean trench wall, keyed to its key — one ledge per identity, never shared. The sensor scoops umber sediment from the ledge; its mineral mix is unique, and the registry's next depth challenge is folded from the last sediment reading plus the key, so a replayed one fails. A copied sensor reads the wrong ledge's pressure. A farm wanting 5,000 fakes must lower 5,000 sensors at $480 apiece — $2.4 million and 150,000 submersible-hours — one dive per ledge, with no bulk order reserving a second ledge.
